svg.title: On an H100, each memory tier trades capacity for speed
svg.desc: The H100 memory hierarchy runs from per-thread registers, the fastest and smallest tier, through per-SM shared memory (SRAM) and a 50 MB shared L2 cache, to 80 GB of HBM3 at about 3.35 TB/s. HBM3 holds model weights and the KV cache and is the bandwidth bottleneck; FlashAttention and kernel fusion reduce HBM traffic by keeping intermediate work in SRAM instead of round-tripping through HBM3.

text.font-family: Space Grotesk, IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: On an H100, each memory tier trades capacity for speed

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: Registers and SRAM sit on-chip, close to compute; HBM3 is off-chip, large, and the bandwidth bottleneck.
